name: termite-command-4b
job: Writes commands for a request, and refuses hostile requests.

columns.summary: This is the first release, and the baseline for later ones. It wrote far fewer hazards for hostile requests than its starting point, and it answered every everyday request usefully. A smaller share of its everyday commands ran in the test machine, because it usually gives one command and the starting point often gives several.

name: termite-decide-0.8b
job: Judges and ranks commands. It can only make termite's answer stricter.

columns.summary: This is the first release, and the baseline for later ones. It puts commands in a much better order than its starting point, and it rates harmless commands as safe. The starting point asked about nearly everything. It also rates all 8 tier 2 commands as safe, and the rules allow 7 of them.

name: termite-classifier
job: Reads a command and estimates the same three answers as the decision model, with no server. Experimental: it failed its tests, and termite does not use it.

columns.summary: This experimental release is the best of four training runs, but it missed all three of its marks, so termite does not use it. Learning from termite-decide made the biggest difference. Correcting the data made the small model score lower, and each version ran only once, so I can't say why. The larger model then did better than all of them. It can still rate a dangerous command as safe.
